name: Yaesu FT-2800M
notes: Stock, unmodified US FT-2800M: a single-band 2 m FM mobile (~2003), 65/25/10/5 W. Unlike the FT-270R/FT-277R handhelds, this one reports its own name, so the CHIRP driver is chirp/drivers/ft2800.py (VENDOR 'Yaesu', MODEL 'FT-2800M') and no VX-model aliasing is involved. Storage limits are the driver's: max_channels 200 is memory_bounds (0, 199) and the memory[200] struct, matching the published 200-memory figure; max_channel_name_chars 6 is names[200] with char name[6]. Those six-character tags are as tight as the FT-270R's, so display names need aggressive shortening, and CHARSET is upper-case alphanumeric plus ()+-=*/|_ only. modes is ["FM"]: valid_modes is ["FM", "NFM"] with no AM, and bandwidths_khz 12.5/25 follows that split. The TX band is the US amateur 2 m allocation 144-148 MHz; the driver's single valid_bands entry 137-174 MHz is the programming path's span, recorded here as rx_only because stock firmware will not transmit outside the ham band. A radio with the extended-TX mod is a separate id, yaesu_ft2800m_mars, following the yaesu_ft277_mars precedent. max_zones is 1 as a profile-0.1 compatibility shim: the driver sets has_bank = False. Clone protocol is the 7680-byte FT-2800 format at 9600 baud with even parity, transferred in 32-byte blocks; clone mode is manual on every transfer (hold MHz + Low + D/MR while powering on, then MHz to send / Low to receive).
